subject: Private Offer & Channel Margin — AWS/GCP packaging questions
messages:
From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@cloudsphere.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer for CloudSphere — AWS + GCP questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at CloudSphere is ready to move forward but we have two parallel asks before we can sign:

1) Private offers on AWS and GCP — we need to understand how Redwood handles channel margin inside a marketplace private offer. Will the reseller (our channel partner) be able to take a margin on top of the private-offer price, or does the marketplace flow require the margin to be baked into the private-offer unit price?

2) SKU/packaging — we’d like a recommended SKU for committed capacity vs open token-based billing. Our finance team prefers a single committed SKU they can charge to their cost center through the marketplace chargeback. Can you advise on packaging best practices for both AWS and GCP marketplaces?

Attached is our RFP extract that includes expected usage (projected first-year spend).

Appreciate a quick note on options and any constraints (reseller billing, invoice flow, DoA approvals). If it helps, include your channel lead and marketplace contact.

Thanks,
Alyssa Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
CloudSphere

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private offer for CloudSphere — AWS + GCP questions

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (channel) and Karthik (marketplace) to confirm operational details. High-level answers up front so you can share with finance:

- Reseller margin: marketplace private offers generally allow the seller to set pricing, and the reseller margin can be handled two ways: (a) reseller is the billing entity and invoices CloudSphere directly (common for AWS Marketplace with a reseller onboarding), or (b) the private-offer price is set such that Redwood pays the reseller a commission outside the marketplace flow. Both are possible but they have different procurement/legal flows.

- Packaging: for committed spend we recommend a reserved-commit SKU (12- or 24-month term) that maps to vCPU/GPU or token-commit depending on your preference; for variable usage we can offer per-token SKUs. Committed SKUs reduce unit price and make budgeting easier for chargeback.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm our standard margin ranges and any limits for private offers (AWS/GCP differences)? I’ve attached our sample private-offer doc to expedite.

Jonas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private offer for CloudSphere — AWS + GCP questions

Hi Alyssa — quick note from channel ops:

- Typical starting channel margin for marketplace private offers is 15–25% off list depending on term and commitment. For a 12mo committed SKU we can usually allow 20% list margin; for enterprise committed bookings (>$500k ARR) we can go higher on a case-by-case basis.

- AWS specifics: if the reseller is set up as the seller-of-record or as a reseller under AWS SA, they can take margin on their invoice. If Redwood needs to remain seller-of-record, we can set the private-offer price lower and pay a separate channel commission — that requires a partner contract and our finance ops to set up the payout schedule (monthly/quarterly).

- GCP Marketplace has similar mechanisms but fewer resellers use the reseller-of-record path; payout timelines and billing reconciliation are typically longer (30–60 days).

Operational asks we’ll need to proceed:
- Confirm preferred billing flow (reseller invoices vs Redwood invoices + commission)
- Term length and expected first-year ARR
- Any compliance/PO terms required by procurement

I attached the channel margin matrix with our typical bands. Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through options.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Channel Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachment: channel_margin_matrix.xlsx

Thanks, Marissa — helpful. Procurement has run the numbers and the ask from our side:

- We can accept a reseller margin of 15% if Redwood will enable the reseller billing flow (reseller invoices CloudSphere directly through AWS).
- Term: 12 months committed SKU (we prefer a vCPU-based reserved SKU mapped to peak concurrency).
- First-year expected spend: $425,000 (see RFP).

Open legal items: requirement for Redwood to include data residency clause and an indemnity paragraph we’ll provide. Also we need confirmation that the reseller can issue invoices that our chargeback system will accept (line-item SKU + charge codes).

If 15% reseller billing flow is acceptable, procurement can draft PO and we’ll start legal redlines. Please confirm and share the private-offer template we should sign.

Best,
Alyssa

1) Channel margin: Redwood accepts the reseller billing flow with a 15% reseller margin. We will onboard the reseller as appropriate in AWS Marketplace so they can be the invoicing party for CloudSphere.

2) Packaging: we will create a 12-month reserved SKU mapped to vCPU-equivalent units per your request. That SKU will be exposed in the AWS private offer and include the SKU code required for CloudSphere chargeback.

3) Legal & compliance: we will accept the requested data residency clause (EU/US region options) and will review the indemnity wording. Please send the redlines to legal@redwood.ai.

4) Operational items: I’ve copied aws-marketplace-sales to confirm reseller onboarding steps and whether any additional approvals are needed on the AWS side. Karthik will start the private-offer creation in parallel and will attach the template.
